# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Old and New Systems Running in Parallel

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in three phases, using a dual-run architecture where both systems remain live and reconciled throughout the migration. The old system is retained in a fully operational, unmodified state through the entire migration and is only considered for retirement in a separate phase after 100% of users have been successfully migrated and validated.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (5% of users — 2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including a successful shadow-mode run against 30 days of replayed production billing events with output parity ≥99.9%; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end at least once.

**Cohort selection:** Internal accounts, employees, and opted-in low-risk external users (e.g., non-annual, low-transaction-volume accounts). No enterprise or high-ARPU accounts.

**Activities:**
- Migrate billing records and payment method tokens for the cohort.
- Run both systems in parallel: new system is authoritative for the migrated cohort, old system continues invoicing/collections for everyone else.
- Daily reconciliation of invoices, charges, and balances between old and new systems for migrated users.
- Support team briefed and on standby; dedicated Slack/incident channel open.

**Duration:** Minimum 7 days before proceeding.

**Exit criterion:** Reconciliation mismatch rate <0.1%, no critical billing incidents (double-charge, failed charge, data loss), support ticket volume for migrated cohort within 1.5x baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (35% of users — 14,000 additional users, 40% cumulative)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Engineering and Finance; any P1/P2 defects found in Phase 1 are resolved and verified; rollback tested again against the larger data shape if schema changes were made.

**Cohort selection:** Broaden to include mid-tier accounts across all customer segments and geographies, still excluding largest enterprise/strategic accounts. Migrate in sub-batches of ~2,000–3,000 users per day/every few days rather than all at once, to preserve the ability to pause between batches.

**Activities:**
- Continue parallel run and daily reconciliation, now at higher volume.
- Enable automated reconciliation alerting (not just manual daily review).
- Weekly review of dunning, refunds, tax calculation, and proration edge cases specifically (common billing migration failure points).
- Customer communications sent ahead of each sub-batch migration.

**Duration:** Minimum 2–3 weeks, paced in sub-batches.

**Exit criterion:** Reconciliation mismatch rate remains <0.1% sustained over the full phase, payment success rate for migrated users within 0.5 percentage points of the old system's baseline, zero unresolved P1 incidents.

---

## Phase 3: Full Rollout (60% remaining users — 24,000 users, 100% cumulative)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; Finance has reconciled at least one full monthly billing cycle end-to-end for the Phase 2 cohort with no material discrepancies; capacity testing confirms the new system can handle full production load with headroom.

**Cohort selection:** All remaining users, including largest enterprise/strategic accounts, migrated last given their complexity and contractual sensitivity. Migrate in sub-batches (e.g., 10–15 batches) with enterprise accounts migrated individually with dedicated account-team support.

**Activities:**
- Continue parallel run through at least one full billing cycle after the last batch is migrated.
- Full reconciliation of the last batch specifically, plus a global reconciliation across all 40,000 users.
- Old system remains fully operational and untouched — no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning occurs in this phase.

**Duration:** Migration itself may complete within 2–4 weeks, but parallel run continues at least one additional full billing cycle beyond the final batch before Phase 3 is considered closed.

**Exit criterion:** 100% of users migrated, reconciliation mismatch rate <0.1% sustained across one full billing cycle for all users, no open P1/P2 billing defects.

---

## Phase 4 (Separate, Post-Migration): Legacy Decommission

Explicitly separated from Phase 3 per requirements. Only begins after Phase 3 exit criteria are met and a full audit/finance sign-off is complete. Includes: read-only archival of old system data, formal stakeholder sign-off, then staged disabling of write access, followed by decommissioning on a separate timeline (not detailed further here, as it is out of scope for the migration rollout itself).

---

## Halt / Rollback Metric

**Automatic halt trigger:** If the billing reconciliation mismatch rate between old and new systems exceeds **0.5%** of migrated users' transactions in any rolling 24-hour window, OR if failed/duplicate payment charges exceed **0.2%** of migrated transactions in a rolling 24-hour window, the rollout is immediately paused, no further users are migrated into the next batch/phase, and the incident is escalated to Billing Engineering and Finance leads for root-cause analysis before resuming.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double charges occur when both systems attempt to bill the same migrated user | Implement a hard mutual-exclusion flag per account so only one system is authoritative for billing at any time, verified by automated pre-charge checks | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate correctly, causing failed charges for migrated users | Run a token-migration validation pass with test authorizations before cutover and reconcile token status daily during each phase | Payments Platform Owner
RISK: Tax, proration, or dunning logic differs subtly between old and new systems, causing incorrect invoice amounts | Run parallel invoice generation and diff old vs. new invoices for every migrated account before finalizing each batch | Finance Systems Analyst
RISK: Enterprise/high-ARPU accounts experience contract-specific billing terms not supported by the new system | Migrate enterprise accounts last, with manual contract-term validation and dedicated account-team review per account | Enterprise Billing Manager
RISK: Rollback becomes infeasible mid-phase due to accumulated data drift between systems | Enforce daily reconciliation with automated alerts and cap batch size so any single failed batch can be rolled back within one business day | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 3
